newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam urges his warplanes and gunners to resist.
newsitem.headline: Saddam urges his warplanes and gunners to resist.

text.p: Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, in a defiant speech on Tuesday, urged his warplanes and anti-aircraft gunners to attack U.S. and allied planes policing air exclusion zones in the southern and northern parts of Iraq.

"You men of our air defence, consider their damned imaginary lines north of the 36th parallel and south of the 32nd parallel non-existent and hit back with capability and efficiency, depending on the Almighty, (at) any hostile plane violating the airspace of your country now and in future," Saddam said in a speech carried live on Iraqi television and radio.
Saddam also called on his troops to resist the United States, urging them to give Washington "a new lesson in the meanings which they (Americans) with their empty...souls do not carry".

Saddam said God "humiliated the aggression and the aggressors", stressing that Iraqi losses were minimal. "The sons of Iraq were on their guard for the aggressors, downing a great number of their missiles," he said. He did not say how many U.S. cruise missiles were shot down.
